title: Heterogeneity of quality of life in the later stages of first-episode psychosis recovery
cohort_overlap_notes: Secondary analysis of the same randomised sample as killackey2019 (ACTRN12608000094370, n = 146 randomised); cites killackey2019 as reference 11.
notes: Contributes one result: 37 of 100 currently in paid work at the 18-month follow-up (Table 1, p. 773). Whole trial-derived cohort (54 IPS, 46 TAU) but the cohort is employment-selected, so it cannot enter the primary pool. The three QoL clusters (31/48/21) are cluster memberships, NOT prevalences, and are not recorded as results.

title: Individual placement and support for vocational recovery in first-episode psychosis: randomised controlled trial
cohort_overlap_notes: Parent trial report for clarke2023. TRIAGE HINT CONFIRMED from both papers: same registry number ACTRN12608000094370, same 146 randomised, same EPPIC site, same 18-month assessment schedule.
notes: Contributes two arm-level results at 6 months (47/66 IPS, 29/60 TAU). Employment counts at 6-12 and 12-18 months are NOT printed: only odds ratios, p-values and a figure of predicted probabilities, so no count is recoverable at any landmark horizon from this report.

title: A 20-Year multi-followup longitudinal study assessing whether antipsychotic medications contribute to work functioning in schizophrenia
cohort_overlap_notes: Same participants as jones2024 (Chicago Follow-up Study / Chicago Longitudinal Research Program). harrow2017 analyses 139 of the cohort, jones2024 analyses 256; the two analysis samples overlap and must never be pooled.
notes: Contributes two 20-year subgroup counts (9/36 on antipsychotics, 16/22 not on antipsychotics). The construct is NOT paid employment: carers of dependents and half-time students are scored as working, and paid work counts only at half-time or more, so it is coded vocational_activity. The manifest's '25/58 at 20y' is a cross-subgroup sum the paper never prints and is not written as a result.

title: Using latent class analysis to investigate enduring effects of intersectional social disadvantage on long-term vocational and financial outcomes in the 20-year prospective Chicago Longitudinal Study
cohort_overlap_notes: Same cohort as harrow2017; CONFIRMED from the Parent study section (CLRP, two Chicago hospitals, index hospitalisation plus six follow-ups at approximately 2, 4.5, 7.5, 10, 15 and 20 years), which cites Harrow, Jobe, Faull & Yang 2017.
notes: NO employment count at any timepoint. Work is reported only as mean Strauss-Carpenter and Harrow Functioning Interview scores by latent class and as GEE coefficients. The latent class sizes (105/73/78) are class memberships, NOT a prevalence, and are not recorded as results (Table 1, p. 2448; Table 2, p. 2450).

title: The relationship between cognitive functioning, age and employment in people with severe mental illnesses in an urban area in India: A longitudinal study
cohort_overlap_notes: Cognitive report of the same 150-participant Pune public-hospital cohort as khare2022b (formerly staged as unknown2022); same inclusion criteria, same site, same 11-13 month follow-up window.
notes: linked_report: the result used for pune_public at 12 months comes from khare2022b, whose analysis population (107) is larger and whose figure is for the whole cohort rather than age subgroups. This report does print its own counts, in the MoCA subsample split at the median age: employed 21/66 younger and 29/67 older at baseline (Table 4, p. 4) and 24/51 younger and 22/43 older at follow-up (Table 5, p. 5). Those are age-subgroup arms on different denominators, so they are named here rather than summed.

title: A 1-Year Prospective Study of Employment in People With Severe Mental Illnesses Receiving Public Sector Psychiatric Services in India
cohort_overlap_notes: Same 150-participant cohort as khare2022. This is the employment article of the pair; khare2022 is its cognitive companion.
notes: STAGED AS unknown2022 AND AS A SUPPLEMENT: the PDF is the full article (Psychiatric Rehabilitation Journal 2022;45(3):237-246, doi 10.1037/prj0000512), not supplementary material. report_id, first_author, doi and title corrected in manifest_changes.csv. Contributes the only result in batch F04 that reaches a landmark horizon: 53 of 107 in paid work at 12 months, derived from two printed cells of the baseline-by-follow-up table.
